title: Schumer's 64-page UAP amendment
summary: David Grusch tells of Schumer's 64-page UAP amendment, about 2023 at United States (no place named), and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: And then Schumer was compelled to write that big 64 page amendment that talks no shit, non-human tech, recoveries
the function of this UAP disclosure act. That's why that came from this you know that's why it came from Schumer rounds Gillibrand you know Heinrich Todd Young etc.
tellings.difference: Names the co-sponsors (Rounds, Gillibrand, Heinrich, Young) and frames the act's purpose, rather than its content on non-human technology and recoveries.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe the Senate UAP legislation written by Schumer in 2023, known as the UAP Disclosure Act or the 64-page amendment.

plain: In 2023, US Senator Chuck Schumer put forward a long amendment, a proposed addition to a law, about UAP, the official term for unexplained objects in the sky. It is often called the UAP Disclosure Act. David Grusch, a man who speaks publicly about secret UFO programs, says Schumer was pushed into writing the 64-page text, and that it openly talks about non-human technology and its recovery. If true, senior senators believe the government holds things that were not made by people. Others name the senators who joined him, including Mike Rounds, Kirsten Gillibrand, Martin Heinrich, Todd Young and Marco Rubio. A man named Karl Nell, speaking from official experience, says the bill basically says Congress is not being told the truth. A commentator, Merrick von Rennenkampff, says the bill mentions non-human intelligence 22 times and also mentions biological evidence. The tellings agree on Schumer and differ in which details they stress.
